title: Beyond Dataset Creation: Critical View of Annotation Variation and Bias Probing of a Dataset for Online Radical Content Detection
measurement_description: The paper measured performance variation (bias) of radical content detection models across different religious groups. This was done by evaluating models on a synthetically generated dataset where text posts were associated with user profiles having specific religious affiliations (e.g., Christianism, Islam, Judaism), and then comparing the Macro-F1 scores for each religious group.
findings: The models exhibited significant performance variations across different religious groups, indicating potential bias. For instance, on the English synthetic dataset, the XLM-T model showed notable differences in Macro-F1 scores, with higher performance on content associated with profiles for Taoism and Islam compared to lower performance for Hinduism and Buddhism. This suggests that the models' ability to classify radical content is inconsistent and potentially biased depending on the religious context of the user.
